recommendation: Aim for roughly 10-20 hard sets per muscle per week; more volume tends to add muscle, with smaller gains per extra set.
why: A meta-analysis of 15 studies found each extra weekly set added about 0.37% muscle size, and a trial in trained men found 30 sets beat 6. A larger preprint meta-regression suggests diminishing returns between 10 and 20 sets.

positions.stance: More weekly volume keeps producing more hypertrophy
positions.best_counterargument: Gains per set shrink at higher volumes and recovery costs rise.

positions.stance: Gains level off around 10-20 weekly sets
positions.best_counterargument: The main support is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed.

positions.stance: Invented position with no real support

what_would_change_this: Well-powered trials in trained women comparing 12 vs 24+ weekly sets.
applies_to_you: As a trained woman with 3 years of training, you are closer to the trained populations studied, but most volume trials studied men.
practical_protocol: Start at about 12 sets per muscle per week split over your 4 days, taking sets to 1-3 reps short of failure, and add sets only if progress stalls and recovery is good.
